questions.question: Explain fairness as a journalistic principle
questions.solution_html:
• Fairness requires journalists to explore and present all sides of a story. This means giving equal
  • opportunity for different perspectives to be heard, especially in contentious or complex issues.
  • Journalists should prioritize truth and transparency over speed or popularity, ensuring the public
  • receives trustworthy content.

questions.question: State three advantages of using smartphones for reporting.
questions.solution_html:
• Smartphones allow journalists to quickly record high-quality photos, videos, and audio, making it
  • easier to document events as they unfold. Smartphones combine camera, editing apps
  • communication tools, and publishing platforms in one device, streamlining the entire reporting
  • process.

questions.question: Analyse why fact-checking is crucial in the digital news environment.
questions.solution_html:
• Analyse why fact-checking is crucial in the digital news environment
  • Fact-checking helps prevent the viral spread of falsehoods that can mislead the public. In a fast-paced
  • digital environment, maintaining trust is essential. Fact-checking ensures that journalists uphold
  • integrity and accuracy, reinforcing public confidence in their reporting. Digital journalism benefits
  • from tools like reverse image searches, geolocation, and AI-assisted verification. These technologies
  • enhance the ability to detect and correct misinformation efficiently.
questions.final_answer: enhance the ability to detect and correct misinformation efficiently

questions.question: What is indepth journalism
questions.solution_html:
• In-depth journalism involves extensive research and reporting to uncover the full scope of a story.
  • Journalists dig deep into facts, data, and sources to provide a comprehensive understanding of
  • complex issues. It goes beyond surface-level reporting by offering background, context, and expert
  • analysis. This helps readers grasp the significance and implications of the story.
questions.final_answer: analysis. This helps readers grasp the significance and implications of the story

questions.question: Elaborate the idea of citizen media and its growing salience in the / present
questions.solution_html:
• Elaborate the idea of citizen media and its growing salience in the present
  • Citizen media allows everyday people—not just professional journalists—to report news, share
  • opinions, and document events using smartphones, blogs, and social platforms. This democratizes
  • information and gives voice to underrepresented communities. Real-Time, On-the-Ground Reporting
  • It amplifies Marginalized Voices and fuelled by Technology and social media. As citizen media grows
  • mainstream outlets are adapting by incorporating user-generated content and engaging with
  • grassroots narratives. It’s reshaping how news is sourced, verified, and consumed

questions.question: In the world of media, images can make or break a news. Discuss
questions.solution_html:
• In the world of media, images can make or break a news. Discuss
  • Images evoke emotions faster than words. A powerful photo can stir empathy, outrage, or hope
  • making the story more compelling and memorable. It enhances comprehension, authenticates the
  • story. Manipulated images can distort facts, sensationalize events, or reinforce bias. Ethical image
  • selection is crucial to maintain journalistic integrity. In the age of social media, striking visuals are
  • more likely to be clicked, shared, and remembered. They often determine whether a story goes viral
  • or gets ignored.
